bills.title: Hog fuel/tax exemption
bills.description: Changing the expiration date for the sales and use tax exemption of hog fuel to comply with the 2045 deadline for fossil fuel-free electrical generation in Washington state and to protect jobs with health care and retirement benefits in economically distressed communities.

bills.title: Leasehold tax/arenas
bills.description: Exempting certain leasehold interests in arenas with a seating capacity of more than 2,000 from the leasehold excise tax.

bills.title: Petroleum storage tanks
bills.description: Creating a state financial assurance program for petroleum underground storage tanks.

bills.title: Aircraft maintenance/tax
bills.description: Concerning retail sales tax exemptions for certain aircraft maintenance and repair.

bills.title: Senior living meals/tax
bills.description: Clarifying that meals furnished to tenants of senior living communities as part of their rental agreement are not subject to sales and use tax.

bills.title: Dairy, etc. tax preferences
bills.description: Extending tax preferences for dairy, fruit and vegetable, and seafood processors.

bills.title: Cultural access programs/tax
bills.description: Modifying the sales and use tax for cultural access programs by allowing the tax to be imposed by a councilmanic or commission authority and defining timelines and priorities for action.

bills.title: Internet projects/tribes
bills.description: Providing a sales and use tax exemption related to internet and telecommunications infrastructure projects involving a federally recognized Indian tribe.

bills.title: Energy/tax
bills.description: Supporting clean energy through tax changes that increase revenue to local governments, schools, and impacted communities.

bills.title: Asphalt & agg. valuation
bills.description: Establishing a method of valuing asphalt and aggregate used in public road construction for purposes of taxation.

bills.title: Medicaid/B&O tax deductions
bills.description: Continuing the business and occupation tax deduction  for federal funds received from a medicaid transformation or demonstration project or medicaid quality improvement program or standard.

bills.title: CCA tax exemptions
bills.description: Creating business and occupation and public utility tax exemptions for certain amounts received as the result of receipt, generation, purchase, sale, transfer, or retirement of allowances, offset credits, or price ceiling units under the climate commitment act.

bills.title: Main street tax credits
bills.description: Allowing main street programs to use remaining main street tax credits after a certain date.

bills.title: County hospital funding
bills.description: Concerning county hospital funding.

bills.title: Public facility districts
bills.description: Concerning public facility districts created by at least two city or county legislative authorities.

bills.title: Employee ownership
bills.description: Concerning employee ownership.

bills.title: Cooperative finance org. B&O
bills.description: Reauthorizing the business and occupation tax deduction for cooperative finance organizations.

bills.title: Newspaper publishers/tax
bills.description: Providing tax relief for newspaper publishers.

bills.title: Complex rehab. products/tax
bills.description: Providing a sales and use tax exemption for mobility enhancing equipment for use by or for a complex needs patient.

bills.title: Alternative jet fuel
bills.description: Promoting the alternative jet fuel industry in Washington.

bills.title: Problem gambling
bills.description: Concerning problem gambling.

bills.title: Child care tax preference
bills.description: Reducing the costs associated with providing child care.

bills.title: Existing structures/housing
bills.description: Providing a sales and use tax incentive for existing structures. (REVISED FOR ENGROSSED: Concerning housing affordability tax incentives for existing structures.)

notes: SHB 1756 is counted as a tax increase although its six-year state estimate (+$950,000) falls just under the $1 million threshold.

Two bills without a state revenue estimate are counted as tax increases because they expand local taxing authority: HB 1575, which lets city and county councils impose the cultural access sales tax without a public vote, and SHB 2348, which creates a county hospital levy outside the usual property tax limits.
